# Legacy DataSet schema

> Generated by `tools/` from the inputs in `source/`. Every statement below is backed by assembly metadata, IL, or a supplied export sample.
> Anything that could not be proven from those inputs is marked **Unknown** rather than guessed.

Spec v3 section 16. Read from each sample's own embedded XSD, so the table and
column lists are **Verified**; the meaning ascribed to a column is only as
strong as its stated evidence.

## Control tables

Export-session bookkeeping and importer instructions rather than payload.

| Table | Columns | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `$Data_FieldDefDbNames` | 3 | FieldDef id -> physical column name. |
| `$Data_TypeDefDbNames` | 2 | TypeDef id -> physical table name. |
| `$DeletedRecords` | 11 | Tombstones so the importer can propagate deletions. |
| `$Header` | 7 | Provenance: source database, core version, export time, page count. |
| `$IdEmbeddingFields` | 4 | Per-column ID remap instructions. |
| `$RootSelection` | 11 | The nodes the operator picked in the export tree. |
| `$Selection` | 11 | The full closure exported after reference expansion. |
| `$basicInfoRelation` | 6 | Relation rows in the shared-infrastructure scope. |
| `$spl_EorgCenter` | 7 | Centre id scope; carries IsImported. |
| `$spl_EorgType` | 10 | Type id scope. |

## Dynamic naming

`dyn_*` and `m0*_*` table names are not stable across systems. The package
carries `$Data_TypeDefDbNames` and `$Data_FieldDefDbNames` to resolve a TypeDef
or FieldDef id to its physical table and column. A reader that hard-codes a
`dyn_` name will break on the next system.

The AiExport profile corroborates this from the other side: each of its record
types declares the legacy table it comes from, and `JsonExportDocumentBuilder`
loads `LoadTableNameByLocalId` / `LoadDataTypeDefInfo` / `LoadDataFieldDefInfo`
from exactly these control tables.

Full machine-readable inventory: `index/legacy-dataset-tables.json`.
